subject: Reserved GPU pool performance validation + commercial terms
messages:
From: Tara Desai <tara@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity questions + target throughput

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. The team had two follow-ups before we can finalize an internal ask: 1) we need validated throughput numbers for an inference flow that averages ~450ms per request (text-generation, 1.5k-token window); 2) commercial — what committed pool sizes you recommend and the unit economics for 12 vs 24 month commits.

Our initial goal is a production SLO of p95 latency under 350ms and sustained ~400 TPS during weekday peak (US hours). Can Redwood prove this with a short load test and share traces/dashboards? Also please confirm what cost and discount tiers look like for reserved pools (monthly equivalent).

Tara
VP Product, Acme Retail
Acme Retail — tara@acme-retail.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tara Desai <tara@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity questions + target throughput

Thanks Tara — we can run a targeted validation and provide a combined TPS + latency report (dashlink + raw CSV) plus kernel-level traces. Neha will own the sizing recommendation; Rafael will capture the commercial alternatives.

Quick ask before we start: can you share a short sample prompt distribution (percentile token lengths) and an example request rate pattern (5m rolling, peak window)? If you prefer, we can run two scenarios: the 400 TPS steady-state and a 1-minute burst to 1k TPS to validate autoscaling/burst behavior.

I’ll schedule an internal run tomorrow and aim to get results by Tue EOD.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Load test plan + expected pool sizing

Team — plan for tomorrow's validation run:
- Workload: mix of 70% short prompts (avg 150 tokens), 20% medium (avg 650 tokens), 10% long (avg 1400 tokens).
- Target scenarios: 400 TPS sustained (30m window), 1k TPS 60s burst, and a 10k-request soak at lower TPS to check mem/KV stability.
- Environment: Reserved pool emulation using 6 x A10G-like instances (we'll run on Redwood Dedicated test cluster), avg batch size tuned to keep p95 inference time close to model kernel baselines.
- Observability: we will collect: per-worker GPU utilization, per-request latencies, KV cache hit-rates, and aggregated TPS. Artifacts: acme_tps_summary.csv, loadtest-traces-20260810.zip. Dash link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ACME/loadtest-20260810

Preliminary expectation: 6 instance reserved pool should comfortably achieve 400 TPS with p95 < 300ms based on prior runs; 1k TPS burst expected to be OK if autoscale/burst capacity is allowed for short windows — sustained 1k will require ~12-instance pool.

Neha
Director, Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Tara Desai <tara@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Load test results + artifacts (ACME scenario)

Tara / Jordan — attaching the results from today's run. Highlights:
- 400 TPS sustained scenario (30m): p50=62ms, p95=278ms, p99=420ms; average GPU util ~= 72%; KV cache hit-rate 56%.
- 1k TPS 60s burst: system sustained burst with p95=410ms; latency tail tightened after cold-KV warmup.
- Sustained 1k TPS: we stopped early — required ~12 instances to keep p95 < 350ms for long-run.

Files attached: acme_tps_summary.csv, loadtest-traces-20260810.zip (contains per-request traces and kernel timings). Dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ACME/loadtest-20260810

Summary recommendation: for Acme's SLO (p95 < 350ms at 400 TPS steady), a 6-instance reserved pool with a short burst allowance to 12 instances for occasional spikes is a cost-efficient starting point. If Acme wants sustained 1k TPS without burst, plan for a 12-instance committed pool.

Next: Rafael — can you put two commercial options (6-instance commit vs 12-instance commit) with monthly equivalents and discount tiers?

Neha
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tara Desai <tara@acme-retail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: two reserved-pool options (draft)

Tara — attached is a short commercial proposal (redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf) and a CSV with cost math. Headline options:

Option A — Starter commit (6-instance pool)
- Configuration: 6x A10G-equivalent GPUs, pinned model (open-llm-v2), autoscale burst window allowed up to 12 instances for up to 5 minutes per 1H without additional charge.
- Price (list): $48,000 / month
- 12-month commit: 15% discount => $40,800 / month (annual invoicing available)
- 24-month commit: 20% discount => $38,400 / month
- SLA: 99.5% uptime, p95 latency credit if missed (0.5% monthly credit per breach; cap 5%)

Option B — Performance commit (12-instance pool, for sustained 1k TPS)
- Configuration: 12x A10G-equivalent GPUs, dedicated capacity, higher cache allocation.
- Price (list): $92,000 / month
- 12-month commit: 18% discount => $75,440 / month
- 24-month commit: 22% discount => $71,760 / month
- SLA: 99.8% uptime; performance credit structure negotiable.

Comments: The burst allowance is included in Option A to match your stated traffic profile; sustained 1k TPS is materially more expensive because of linear GPU cost at scale. We can offer a 6-month ramp credit or a short-term intro discount for the first quarter if you need to smooth budgetary approvals.

Rafael Mendes
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Tara Desai <tara@acme-retail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <acme-procurement@example.com>, J. Desai <j.desai@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: two reserved-pool options (draft)

Thanks Rafael — helpful breakdown. A few quick items from procurement/Product:
1) Can you move the 12-month discount to 20% on Option A? That gets closer to our internal budget.
2) We need an explicit performance SLA for p95 inference latency (p95 < 350ms) during the committed baseline (400 TPS). If the SLA is missed, we want a 3% monthly credit and a written remediation plan within 48 hours.
3) We'd like DocuSign-ready docs and a one-page mutual action plan that calls out rollout milestones (pilot -> prod -> scale).

If you can confirm on pricing/SLA and get the DocuSign link, procurement can circle back quickly.

Tara
VP Product, Acme Retail
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: approval request — counter to Acme (pricing & SLA)

Team — Acme is pushing for 20% on the 12-month Option A and a firm p95 SLA (p95 < 350ms) with a 3% monthly credit and 48-hour remediation. They will sign quickly if we can meet these terms and provide a DocuSign-ready package + MAP.

Ask: can we approve a counter of 16% discount for 12-month on Option A (i.e., $40,320 / month) with the proposed SLA (3% credit) and a technical addendum that limits the SLA to the committed baseline (400 TPS sustained) and excludes multi-region/network outages? We include a one-time migration credit of one month if they commit 12 months.

If leadership greenlights this, I’ll send a customer-facing DocuSign bundle and loop procurement. Rafael — if you agree, I can present the final pricing.

Jordan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
